title: Promises and the Microtask Queue
concept: Promise then callbacks go into the Microtask Queue and have higher priority than the Task Queue

steps.title: console.log('start')
steps.explanation: The first synchronous line, `console.log('start')`, is added to the call stack and executes immediately.

steps.title: Register setTimeout
steps.explanation: The `setTimeout` callback is delegated to the Web API. Once the timer (0ms) completes, it moves to the **Task Queue** and waits.

steps.title: Register Promise.then
steps.explanation:
The `.then()` callback moves to the **Microtask Queue** and waits.
This is a separate queue with higher priority than the Task Queue.

steps.title: console.log('end')
steps.explanation:
The last synchronous line, `console.log('end')`, executes.
Now the call stack is about to be emptied.

steps.title: Process Microtask (Promise)
steps.explanation:
Once the call stack is empty, the event loop checks the Microtask Queue before the Task Queue.
The Promise callback waiting there moves to the call stack and executes.
steps.keyInsight: The Microtask Queue always has higher priority than the Task Queue.

steps.title: Process Task (setTimeout)
steps.explanation:
Only after the Microtask Queue is completely empty does the event loop check the Task Queue.
The `setTimeout` callback waiting there moves to the call stack and executes last.

quiz.explanation:
Synchronous code (C) → Microtask (B) → Task (A).
Promise then callbacks go into the Microtask Queue, setTimeout goes into the Task Queue, and Microtasks have higher priority.

misconceptions.wrong: setTimeout(fn, 0) and Promise.then() use the same queue
misconceptions.correct: setTimeout uses the Task Queue (Macrotask Queue), while Promise.then() uses the Microtask Queue.
misconceptions.why: The Microtask Queue is always processed before the Task Queue.

misconceptions.wrong: 0ms is shorter, so setTimeout runs first
misconceptions.correct:
The timing doesn't matter.
**Which queue you're in line at** is what counts.
misconceptions.why:
Per the event loop spec, the Task Queue is never executed until the Microtask Queue is completely empty.
If a Microtask gets stuck in an infinite loop, Tasks might never run (starvation).

keyTakeaway: Execution priority: synchronous code > Microtask (Promise) > Task (setTimeout)
